events.title: The death of Pope St. John XXIII
events.shortBlurb: The “Good Pope” who summoned the Second Vatican Council died on the Monday after Pentecost, mourned across the world…
body: On the evening of 3 June 1963, the Monday after Pentecost, Pope John XXIII died in the Vatican, aged eighty-one, of cancer of the stomach. Born Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli at Sotto il Monte near Bergamo in 1881, he had been elected in October 1958 at seventy-six and was widely expected to be a caretaker pope.

Instead he announced, in January 1959, an ecumenical council, and on 11 October 1962 he opened the Second Vatican Council, calling the Church to renewal and to the reading of the signs of the times. His last encyclical, Pacem in Terris of April 1963, was addressed not to the hierarchy alone but to all men of good will.

His death — mourned far beyond the bounds of the Catholic world — ended a pontificate of less than five years that had changed the Church's course. 'Good Pope John' was beatified by John Paul II in 2000 and canonized by Pope Francis on 27 April 2014.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. John XXIII (vatican.va)
